mainTopic: Black, red, and green berries on the הדס; דחוי מעיקרא and נראה ונדחה; fixing the הדס and the לולב binding on יום טוב; and the laws of the ערבה
overview: This amud finishes רבא's objection to an early version of רב חסדא's teaching, and then gives the corrected version. In it, רב, quoted by רב חסדא, says that berries outnumbering the leaves disqualify a הדס only when they are black, since green berries blend in. רב פפא adds that red berries count like black, citing רבי חנינא on blood colors. The גמרא then studies the משנה's rulings that reducing the berries makes the הדס fit, and that one may not reduce them on יום טוב. From the timing of when the berries turned black, it proves that דחוי מעיקרא לא הוי דחוי. It does not prove that נראה ונדחה can become fit again. A ברייתא records רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון permitting the berries to be picked on יום טוב, and the גמרא defends him using דבר שאין מתכוין and פסיק רישיה. Next comes a ברייתא about rewrapping a loosened לולב binding on יום טוב like a vegetable bundle, explained according to רבי יהודה's view that a bow is a real knot. Finally, a new משנה lists which ערבות are פסולה and which are כשרה, and ברייתות explain 'ערבי נחל' and teach that willows from any place are valid.

steps.title: Berries in several spots make the branch look speckled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its objection to the earlier version of רב חסדא's statement. Berries spread over two or three places are worse, not better, because the branch looks speckled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the berries are in two or three places, the branch is speckled, and so it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that began on the previous amud, where רבא objected to רב חסדא. The earlier version of רב חסדא said berries in two or three places are fine, and the objection argues the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier version of רב חסדא said the rule of 'too many berries' applies only when the berries are in one spot. The גמרא says the opposite makes more sense: berries scattered in two or three places make the הדס look patchy and spotted. A spotted look lacks beauty, so it should certainly be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: Speckled or spotted, with patches of different colors
Places or spots on the branch
Unfit for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the tail end of רבא's challenge, begun on the previous amud, against the rejected first version of רב חסדא's statement.

phrases.english: Two or three places
phrases.notes: Berries spread over several spots on the branch

phrases.english: is speckled, and it is unfit.
phrases.notes: A spotted look lacks beauty (הדר)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the אדרבה objection, begun on the previous amud, against the first version of רב חסדא
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רב חסדא: the rule applies only to berries in one spot, so two or three spots are fit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scattered berries make the branch look speckled, which is less beautiful, so they should be more unfit, not fit

steps.title: Correcting what was actually said: back to the משנה's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first version and introduces the correct one. It anchors it on the משנה's case of berries outnumbering leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: 'Or if its berries were more than its leaves, it is unfit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the challenged version and says it will now give the correct version of the teaching. This step sets up the next move by quoting the משנה that the corrected statement explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'אי אתמר הכי אתמר' means the earlier report was mistaken, and the real statement went differently. The גמרא first quotes the line of the משנה that the real statement comments on: berries more numerous than leaves make the הדס unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a correction of a reported teaching)
Berries (on the הדס branch)
More numerous

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
phrases.notes: This replaces the version that was just rejected.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ עֲנָבָיו מְרוּבִּין מֵעָלָיו — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: 'Or if its berries were more numerous than its leaves, it is unfit.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by abandoning the earlier version and starting a corrected one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: the earlier report of the statement was mistaken
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא limited the rule to berries in a single spot
steps.terutzMaskana: The real statement attaches to the משנה's rule and limits it in a different way, given in the next step

steps.title: Only black berries disqualify; green berries are fine
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רב, rules that too many berries disqualify only when the berries are black. Green berries match the הדס and do not disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, and may God help him: They taught this only about black berries. But if its berries are green, they are the same kind as the הדס, and it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the corrected teaching. The משנה's rule about too many berries applies only to black berries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Black berries stand out against green leaves, so the branch looks spotted and loses its beauty. Green berries blend in with the leaves and look like part of the הדס itself. So even when green berries outnumber the leaves, the branch stays fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Our great teacher, meaning רב, the teacher of רב חסדא
And may the Omnipresent help him (a blessing for the teacher)
They taught this only about (a limiting formula)
Black (ripe berries)
Green (unripe berries)

steps.whatToRemember: The problem with too many berries is the spotted look. So the rule applies only to black berries, which contrast with the leaves, and not to green ones.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This statement, our great teacher said it,
phrases.notes: Referring to רב

phrases.english: and may the Omnipresent be his help:
They taught this only when its berries are black.
phrases.notes: Black contrasts with the green leaves

phrases.english: But if its berries are green —
they are of the same kind as the הדס, and it is fit.
phrases.notes: Same color, so the branch is not speckled

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דָּבָר זֶה רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּדוֹל אֲמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the corrected statement introduced in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Berries outnumbering leaves disqualify a הדס only when the berries are black; green berries do not disqualify it
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reason behind the disqualification, which is the speckled look. The rest of the discussion depends on that reason.

steps.title: Red berries count like black berries
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that red berries have the same status as black berries, so they also disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Red berries are like black ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds to רב חסדא's rule. Red berries are treated like black berries, not like green ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only black berries disqualify, someone might think red berries are fine because they are not black. רב פפא says red and black are treated as one color group, and both contrast with green leaves. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Red (berries)
Are similar or equivalent

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Red ones are like black ones,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲדוּמּוֹת כִּשְׁחוֹרוֹת דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב חסדא's black/green rule to red berries
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red berries have the status of black berries and disqualify the הדס when they outnumber the leaves

steps.title: Proof from רבי חנינא: black blood is really red
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports his ruling with רבי חנינא's teaching, from the laws of נדה, that black blood is really red blood that has deteriorated.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא said: This black blood is really red, only it became damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a source to prove that red and black are the same color family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of נדה, רבי חנינא teaches that black blood is red blood that has spoiled or darkened. That shows the Sages saw red and black as two shades of one color. So red berries are treated like black berries.

keyTerms.meaning: Black blood (one of the impure blood colors in the laws of נדה)
That was damaged or deteriorated

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chanina said:
This black blood — it is really red,
phrases.notes: This comes from the laws of נדה.

phrases.english: except that it became damaged.
phrases.notes: Red and black are shades of one color

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב פפא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: Red berries have the same status as black berries
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא in the laws of נדה: black blood is deteriorated red blood
steps.whatToRemember: Black and red berries disqualify when they outnumber the leaves. Green berries do not.

steps.title: New topic in the משנה: reducing the berries makes it fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if he removed berries until they were fewer than the leaves, the הדס is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he reduced them, it is fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. This step sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a הדס with too many berries can be fixed by picking off berries until the leaves are the majority. The גמרא is about to ask when this fixing happened, because the timing matters.

keyTerms.meaning: He reduced them (picked off some berries)
Fit for the מצוה

phrases.english: If he reduced them — it is fit.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section on the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס with too many berries becomes fit once the berries are reduced

steps.title: When were the berries reduced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what point the person removed the extra berries.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reduced them when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the timing of the fix. It is preparing to check two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing matters because the לולב bundle is tied together. If the הדס was unfit when the bundle was tied, there may be a problem even after it is fixed. Each possible answer is checked in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: When?

phrases.english: He reduced them — when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case setting of the משנה line just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the berries were reduced before or after the לולב was tied

steps.title: Before tying the לולב? Too obvious to need saying
steps.stepSummary: If the berries were removed before the לולב was tied, the ruling is obvious, so the משנה would not bother teaching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was before he tied it, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it. If he fixed the הדס before tying the bundle, of course it is fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the berries were removed before tying, the הדס was never unfit while part of the bundle. Nothing in that case is new, so the משנה must be talking about a less obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility to be tested)
He tied it (the לולב bundle)
It is obvious

phrases.english: If you say before he tied it — it is obvious!
phrases.notes: That would teach us nothing new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the berries were removed before the bundle was tied
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling would be obvious, and a משנה does not teach the obvious

steps.title: After tying the לולב? Then it was unfit from the start
steps.stepSummary: If the berries were removed after the לולב was tied, then the bundle was unfit from the moment it was tied, which is a case of דחוי מעיקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was after he tied it. But then it was rejected from the very start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the second option: the berries were reduced after the bundle was tied. That means the הדס was unfit when it was tied. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bundle was tied while the הדס was unfit, the bundle began in a rejected state. That brings up the open question of whether something rejected from the start stays rejected even after it is fixed. Yet the משנה says it is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: After
Rejected from the start: something unfit from the beginning that later becomes fit

steps.confusionAlert: דחוי מעיקרא means the item was never fit at all and only became fit later. It does not mean the item was fit, became unfit, and then became fit again.

phrases.english: Rather, after he tied it —
it is rejected from the start!
phrases.notes: Unfit at the moment of tying

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְבָתַר דְּלֹאגְדֵיהּ — דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the first option was rejected, the משנה must mean after tying. This answers step 7 and sets up the proof of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The berries were reduced after the לולב was tied, so the הדס was unfit at the time of tying (דחוי מעיקרא).

steps.title: So something rejected from the start is not permanently rejected
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה calls the הדס fit even though it was unfit when tied, the גמרא settles the earlier open question: דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve from this: something rejected from the start is not considered rejected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the משנה to answer an open question raised earlier: can something unfit at the start become fit later? The next step pushes this proof away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה must be speaking of reducing the berries after tying, and still it calls the הדס fit. So being unfit at the start does not permanently disqualify the item. This answers the earlier question of whether דחוי מעיקרא counts as a lasting rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve from this (use this source to answer an open question)
Is not considered rejected

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule about דחוי, things rejected from a מצוה and whether they can come back, appears across many areas of הלכה. This משנה is used as a source for one side of the question.

phrases.english: Resolve from this:
rejected from the start — is not considered rejected!

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט מִינַּהּ: דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the problem of step 9 into a proof that answers the earlier question
steps.raayaObject: That דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה rules the הדס fit after the berries are reduced, even though it was unfit when the לולב was tied.

steps.title: Tying the bundle is only a designation, so the proof falls away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 10. The berries were indeed removed after tying, but this view holds that אגד is only a הזמנה, which has no legal weight. So the הדס was never formally rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is a case where he removed the berries after tying it. But this view holds that tying is just a setting aside, and just setting something aside counts for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the proof it just made about דחוי מעיקרא. It explains that the tied bundle was never really 'rejected' in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 assumed that the moment of tying is the 'start' of the מצוה. Here the גמרא says tying is only a הזמנה, a preparation with no legal force. So an unfit הדס at the time of tying was never rejected from a real starting point, and this proof about דחוי מעיקרא falls away. Steps 16–18 prove the point from a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; the opening word for rejecting a suggestion
After he tied it
The tying of the לולב bundle
Mere designation; only setting something aside for a מצוה
It is nothing; it has no legal weight

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does NOT change the facts here. It still agrees the berries were removed after tying. What it changes is how much tying counts, saying it counts for nothing (לאו כלום הוא).

phrases.english: Really, it is after he tied it,
and he holds: tying is merely a designation,
phrases.notes: So tying is not the real starting point of the מצוה.

phrases.english: and mere designation is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the proof drawn in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof about דחוי מעיקרא, not the ruling of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that tying is the legal start of the מצוה. In fact אגד is only a הזמנה, which has no legal weight.

steps.title: The משנה: do not reduce the berries on the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one may not reduce the berries on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not reduce the berries on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. This sets up the next question about what happens if someone did remove them anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing berries on יום טוב is forbidden because it counts as fixing an object (תיקון מנא). The משנה only says 'one may not,' which is the wording of a rule for the first place. That leaves room to ask what happens after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduce / lessen (here, the number of berries)
The festival day

phrases.english: And one may not reduce them on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to remove the berries of a הדס on יום טוב.

steps.title: What if he went ahead and picked them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if someone broke the rule and picked off the berries on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did it anyway and picked them, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the case after the fact: is the הדס usable?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording 'one may not' is only about what to do in the first place. The question checks whether breaking that rule also makes the הדס unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: He went ahead and broke the rule
And picked them (the berries)
What is the law?

phrases.english: But if he went ahead and picked them, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the after-the-fact case implied by step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הדס is כשר if the berries were picked on יום טוב against the rule.

steps.title: It is fit
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the הדס is כשר. The משנה only forbade the act; it did not make the הדס unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that after the fact, the הדס is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה only said 'one may not,' the act is forbidden but the result is valid. This ruling is the base for the next questions about rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit / valid for the מצוה

phrases.english: It is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the fact, the הדס is כשר.

steps.title: When did the berries turn black?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the berries became black, which is the point when they made the הדס unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did they turn black?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the timing of the problem. This sets up two options that will teach about rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Berries only make a הדס unfit once they ripen and outnumber the leaves. The timing tells us whether the הדס was unfit from before יום טוב, or fit at first and only later became unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: That they turned black (ripened)
When?

phrases.english: That they turned black — when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the timing behind the ruling of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the berries turned black before יום טוב or on יום טוב itself.

steps.title: If they were black from yesterday, this proves early rejection is not permanent
steps.stepSummary: Option one: the berries were black from before יום טוב. Then the הדס was דחוי מעיקרא, and since the משנה calls it כשר, we learn that דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they turned black from yesterday, then it was rejected from the start. Then settle from here that being rejected from the start is not a real rejection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first timing option and shows what it would prove. It brings back the proof about דחוי מעיקרא that was lost in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the berries were black before the festival, the הדס was unfit when the מצוה began. Yet the משנה says that once the berries are removed it is כשר. So a הדס that was unfit from the start can become fit, and דחוי מעיקרא is not permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a first option)
From yesterday (before יום טוב)
Rejected from the start: unfit from the very beginning
Settle the question from here

phrases.english: If you say they turned black from yesterday —
it is rejected from the start.
Settle from it
that rejected from the start is not a rejection!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the timing question of step 15 and draws a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: That דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה rules the הדס כשר after the berries are picked, even though it was unfit from before יום טוב.

steps.title: If they turned black on the festival, it proves a rejected item can become fit again
steps.stepSummary: Option two: the berries turned black on יום טוב. Then the הדס was נראה ונדחה, fit at first and then rejected. Since it is כשר, we would learn that it can become fit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that they turned black on יום טוב? Then it was fit and then rejected. Learn from this: fit and then rejected can become fit again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the second timing option. It uses it to try to settle a different open question, נראה ונדחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the berries were still green when יום טוב began, the הדס was fit at the start and became unfit later. The משנה says it is כשר once the berries are picked. That would prove that something fit, then rejected, can return to being fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that…? (pushes toward a second reading)
Fit and then rejected: fit at the start, unfit later
Becomes fit again
Learn from this

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. דחוי מעיקרא means unfit from the very start. נראה ונדחה means fit at first and only later unfit. They are two separate questions.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that they turned black on the festival,
so it is fit and then rejected.
Learn from this:
fit and then rejected — becomes fit again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first timing option with a second one that would prove a bigger point.
steps.raayaObject: That נראה ונדחה can become fit again.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה rules the הדס כשר, read as a case where the berries ripened on יום טוב.

steps.title: No: they were black from before, so only the first point is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof. The berries were black from before יום טוב, so we can prove that דחוי מעיקרא is not a rejection. But we cannot prove anything about נראה ונדחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, they turned black from the start. You can settle from here that rejected from the start is not a rejection. But that fit and then rejected becomes fit again, you cannot settle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof about נראה ונדחה and goes back to the first option. Only the point about דחוי מעיקרא is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה can be read as a case where the berries were black before the festival. On that reading, it only shows that early rejection is not permanent. Since the משנה does not have to be about berries ripening on יום טוב, it gives no proof for נראה ונדחה, and that question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: No (opens the rejection)
From the start (here, before יום טוב)
Do not settle it; the question stays open

steps.whatToRemember: From this משנה we learn that דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection: something unfit from the start can become fit. Whether נראה ונדחה can become fit again remains unproven here.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rules of דחייה, whether something rejected can come back, apply across many areas, such as מצוות and קרבנות. This step shows the גמרא carefully separating the two kinds of rejection.

phrases.english: No, really they turned black from the start,

phrases.aramaic: דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּלָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי תִּפְשׁוֹט מִינַּהּ,
phrases.english: that rejected from the start is not a rejection, settle from it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִרְאֶה וְנִדְחֶה חוֹזֵר וְנִרְאֶה, לָא תִּפְשׁוֹט.
phrases.english: but that fit and then rejected becomes fit again, do not settle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 17 and returns to the reading of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof about נראה ונדחה. It keeps the proof about דחוי מעיקרא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be about berries that were black before יום טוב, so it does not have to be about נראה ונדחה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דחוי מעיקרא is not a permanent rejection. Whether נראה ונדחה can become fit again remains unresolved.

steps.title: A ברייתא: may one remove the extra berries on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא says one may not reduce the berries on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not reduce the berries on יום טוב. In the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון they said: One may reduce them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two opinions about removing berries from a הדס on יום טוב to make it kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that if a הדס has more berries than leaves, removing berries makes it kosher, but this may not be done on יום טוב. The תנא קמא of the ברייתא agrees with the משנה. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון allows it, and the next steps will ask how he can allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
We reduce, meaning we remove some berries so there are fewer berries than leaves.
The festival day.
רבי אליעזר, the son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with steps 14 to 18. Those steps asked whether a הדס that was fixed is now kosher. This ברייתא asks a different question: is the act of removing the berries allowed on יום טוב?

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְמַעֲטִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One may not reduce [the berries] on the Festival.
phrases.notes: This matches the ruling of our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרוּ: מְמַעֲטִין.
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon they said: One may reduce [them].
phrases.notes: This is the opinion the גמרא will now question.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְמַעֲטִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens a new topic: whether the act itself is allowed, not whether the הדס is kosher afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids reducing the berries on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: But removing the berries fixes a usable item on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון. Removing the berries turns an unfit הדס into a fit one, which is מתקן מנא, a forbidden act on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is fixing a vessel on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lenient opinion. How can he permit something that makes the הדס usable on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making an item fit for use on יום טוב is forbidden as מתקן מנא. Removing the berries does exactly that, because it changes the הדס from unfit to fit for the מצוה. So it seems the act should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. An opening word for a challenge.
Fixing or preparing a usable item. This is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָא מְתַקֵּן מָנָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: But he is fixing a vessel on the Festival!
phrases.notes: The 'vessel' here is the הדס, which becomes usable for the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מְתַקֵּן מָנָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the lenient opinion in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון that one may reduce the berries.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing the berries makes the הדס fit. Making an item fit on יום טוב is the forbidden act of מתקן מנא.

steps.title: רב אשי: he picked them to eat, and his father permits an unintended result
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the person picked the berries in order to eat them. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, רבי שמעון, that an unintended result does not make an act forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where he picked them to eat them. And רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who said: an act done without intending the forbidden result is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. The person is not trying to fix the הדס. He just wants to eat the berries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking berries off a detached branch in order to eat them is permitted on יום טוב. The הדס becoming kosher is only a side effect he did not intend. רבי שמעון rules that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, and his son follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from the last generation of the Babylonian Talmud.
For eating.
He holds like his father.
An act whose forbidden result you did not intend.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the ruling about the הדס to רבי שמעון's well-known principle about unintended results.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁלִּקְּטָן לַאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: For example, where he picked them for eating.
phrases.notes: His goal is food, not fixing the הדס.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon holds like his father,
who said: An unintended act is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the famous principle of רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁלִּקְּטָן לַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case (he picked them to eat), combined with the principle of דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought he was removing the berries in order to fix the הדס.
steps.terutzMaskana: His goal was eating. The fixing is an unintended side effect, and רבי שמעון permits that.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון agrees when the result is certain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects using a rule of אביי and רבא. Even רבי שמעון forbids an act whose forbidden result is certain, which is called פסיק רישיה. Here, removing the berries will certainly make the הדס kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer. 'I didn't intend it' only helps when the forbidden result might not happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits an unintended result only when that result is not certain. If you cut off an animal's head, it will certainly die, so you cannot say you did not mean to kill it. Here too, once the berries are removed, the הדס will certainly become kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Two great אמוראים in Babylonia.
Both of them.
Agrees, concedes.
'Cut off its head and will it not die?' This describes a forbidden result that is certain to happen.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'I didn't intend it' always works for רבי שמעון. It does not work when the forbidden result is certain (פסיק רישיה).

phrases.english: But Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'!
phrases.notes: When the result is certain, the act is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges רב אשי's answer in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's use of דבר שאין מתכוין to permit removing the berries.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing the berries will certainly make the הדס kosher. That makes it a פסיק רישיה, which even רבי שמעון forbids.

steps.title: The case is where he has another kosher הדס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the person already has another kosher הדס. So making this one kosher is not a real act of fixing for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he has another הושענא (הדס).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case to save רב אשי's answer. The person already owns another kosher הדס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he already has a kosher הדס for the מצוה, he does not need this one. So the fact that it becomes kosher is not treated as fixing an item for use. Therefore the פסיק רישיה objection does not apply, and eating the berries is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This phrase narrows the case.
Here it means a הדס. The word can also refer to the bundle of the ארבעה מינים.
Another one.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון permits removing the berries on יום טוב only in a narrow case. He picked them to eat, he did not intend to fix the הדס, and he already has another kosher הדס, so the fixing does not count as a forbidden פסיק רישיה.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he has another myrtle.
phrases.notes: He does not need this הדס, so fixing it is not a real act of preparation for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the פסיק רישיה challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Removing the berries certainly fixes a הדס he needs, so it is a forbidden פסיק רישיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He has another kosher הדס, so making this one kosher is not counted as fixing an item. The act is permitted.

steps.title: A loosened לולב binding may be re-wrapped like a vegetable bundle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the binding of the לולב came undone on יום טוב, one may bind it again only by wrapping it, the way vegetables are bundled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If the binding of the לולב came undone on יום טוב, one may bind it again like a bundle of vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about fixing the לולב's binding on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying a real knot is a forbidden מלאכה on יום טוב. So the ברייתא allows only a simple wrap, where the string is wound around the bundle or tucked in, with no knot. This is how people bundle vegetables at the market.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding that holds the לולב, הדסים, and ערבות together
Came undone, got loose
A vegetable bundle, held by winding a string around it with no knot
The festival day, when certain מלאכות such as tying a knot are forbidden

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If its binding came undone on the Festival,
he binds it like a bundle of vegetables.
phrases.notes: He wraps it without tying a real knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּתַּר אַגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from removing the berries of the הדס on יום טוב to a related question: fixing the לולב's binding on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loosened לולב binding may be redone on יום טוב only by wrapping it like a vegetable bundle, with no knot.

steps.title: Why not just tie a bow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא requires a simple wrap, when a bow is normally allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let him tie a bow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. A bow is normally not considered a real knot, so why not use one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bow (עניבה) is a temporary loop, and in general it is not counted as a forbidden knot. If so, the ברייתא seems too strict. A bow would hold better than a simple wrap and should be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A bow, a loop knot that is easy to undo
But why? A formula that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But why?
Let him tie it with a bow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strict ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's requirement to wrap like a vegetable bundle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bow is generally not a forbidden knot, so a better option seems to be available.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who treats a bow as a real knot
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. He holds that a bow is a full knot, so tying one is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says a bow is a full-fledged knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming the author of the ברייתא: רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a bow counts as a real knot. That makes it forbidden on יום טוב. The only option left is a simple wrap with no knot at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Used to identify the author of a source
A full-fledged, real knot

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is רבי יהודה,
who says: a bow
is a full-fledged knot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bow is not a knot, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה a bow is a real knot, so only a wrap is allowed.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה requires a proper binding
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is רבי יהודה, there is a problem. He requires the לולב to have a full, proper binding, and a vegetable-style wrap should not be good enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, he requires a full-fledged binding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. רבי יהודה also holds that the לולב must be properly bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מסכת, רבי יהודה ruled that the לולב must be bound as part of the מצוה, learning this from the bundle of אזוב. A real binding for him needs a real knot. So a loose wrap would make the לולב פסול in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A full, proper binding
Requires

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate rulings of רבי יהודה are in play here. One: a bow counts as a real knot. Two: the לולב must be properly bound for the מצוה. Keep them apart.

phrases.english: If it is רבי יהודה,
he requires a full-fledged binding!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֶגֶד מְעַלַּיְיתָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's other view, that a לולב needs a real binding, contradicts allowing a simple wrap.

steps.title: This תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point only
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the ברייתא agrees with רבי יהודה that a bow is a real knot. He disagrees with him that a לולב needs a real binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא holds like him in one matter and disagrees with him in one matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem. The ברייתא's author follows רבי יהודה on only one of his two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא agrees that a bow is a full knot, which is why he forbids it on יום טוב. He does not agree that binding is required for the מצוה. For him, the binding only makes the מצוה nicer, so a simple wrap is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees with him on one point
Disagrees with him on one point
A sage of the משנה period, here the author of the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, a loose לולב binding is wrapped, not knotted. The ברייתא's author agrees with רבי יהודה that a bow is a real knot, but holds that binding the לולב is only for beauty.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This תנא holds like him in one matter,
and disagrees with him in one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 and closes the topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the view (the תנא partly agrees with רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה fully, so it should require a real binding.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא follows רבי יהודה only about the bow, not about the binding requirement.

steps.title: The משנה lists which ערבות are פסולה and which are כשרה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the defects that make a ערבה פסולה and the lesser defects that still leave it כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ערבה that is stolen or dry is פסולה. One from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is פסולה. If its top was cut off, its leaves were torn off, or it is a צפצפה, it is פסולה. If it is wilted, has lost a few of its leaves, or grew in a rain-watered field, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It covers the third of the four species, the ערבה, and gives its פסול and כשר cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These rules mostly match the earlier ones for לולב and הדס: stolen, dry, and idolatry-related species are פסול. New here is the צפצפה, a plant that looks like a willow but is not one. The ruling that a ערבה from a בעל field is כשרה shows it does not have to grow by a river.

keyTerms.meaning: Willow branch, one of the four species
A tree that is worshipped as idolatry
A city whose people were led into idolatry; its property must be destroyed
A plant similar to a willow, but not a real ערבה
Wilted, slightly dried
Grown in a field watered only by rain, not by a river

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A willow that is stolen or dry is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת — פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: One from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is unfit.
If its top was cut off, or its leaves were torn off,
or if it is the צפצפה, it is unfit.
If it is wilted, or some of its leaves fell off,
or it is from a rain-watered field, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the ערבה, after the earlier discussion of the הדס and the לולב's binding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen, dry, idolatrous, top-cut, or leaf-stripped ערבה, or a צפצפה, is פסולה. A wilted ערבה, one missing a few leaves, or one from a בעל field is כשרה.

steps.title: 'ערבי נחל' means willows that grow by a brook
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the פסוק's phrase 'ערבי נחל' describes willows that grow by a brook.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Willows of the brook' means those that grow by the brook.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that explains the פסוק about the ערבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, 'נחל' tells us where the ערבה usually grows. This sets up the question of whether a ערבה must actually come from a riverbank. The משנה already said a בעל willow is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Willows of the brook,' the words of the פסוק in ויקרא
That grow

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
'Willows of the brook' means those that grow by the brook.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַרְבֵי נַחַל הַגְּדֵילִין עַל הַנַּחַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the new משנה by explaining the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ערבי נחל' refers to willows that grow by a brook.

steps.title: Second reading: a willow whose leaf is long like a brook
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: 'ערבי נחל' describes a willow whose leaf is long and narrow, like a flowing brook.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Willows of the brook' means one whose leaf is drawn out like a brook.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second way to read 'נחל'. This time it describes the leaf's shape, not where the tree grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'נחל' is a description of the plant itself: its leaf is long, like a stream. This fits the משנה's ruling that a willow from a בעל field is כשרה. What matters is that the leaf has the right shape.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
Drawn out, elongated

steps.whyThisMatters: The second reading makes the leaf's shape the identifying sign of a real ערבה. That helps tell it apart from look-alikes such as the צפצפה.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Willows of the brook'
means one whose leaf is elongated like a brook.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ערבי נחל' describes a willow whose leaf is long and narrow like a brook.

steps.title: Are willows not growing by a brook also valid?
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the plain words ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ would only include willows that grow by a brook. It then asks where we learn that willows from a rain-watered field or from the mountains are also valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: From ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ (willows of the brook), I would only know about willows that grow by a brook. Willows of a rain-watered field and willows of the mountains, from where do we know they are valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא. The ברייתא raises a question it is about to answer: are willows that do not grow by a brook also valid? This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read very literally, ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ seems to limit the מצוה to willows that grow next to water. The ברייתא names two other places where willows grow: a בַּעַל field, which is watered only by rain, and the mountains. It asks for a source that these are valid too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
I would only know about (the literal case)
Of a field watered only by rain, with no irrigation
From where do we know?

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עַרְבֵי נַחַל.
phrases.english: "Willows of the brook": I would only know about actual willows of the brook.
phrases.notes: Willows that physically grow beside a brook.

phrases.english: Those of a rain-watered field and those of the mountains, from where do we know they are valid?
phrases.notes: A בַּעַל field gets its water only from rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עַרְבֵי נַחַל. שֶׁל בַּעַל וְשֶׁל הָרִים מִנַּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 30–31 explained what ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ describes. This ברייתא asks whether the phrase limits where the willow must grow.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that willows not growing by a brook, from a בַּעַל field or the mountains, are valid.

steps.title: Willows from any place are valid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק's words ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ include willows from any location.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״, which teaches that willows are valid from any place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The words of the פסוק teach that willows from anywhere, not only from beside a brook, are כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק's wording as including, not limiting. Sefaria explains that the plural form ״עַרְבֵי״ broadens the law to willows from any place. So נַחַל tells us what kind of tree a ערבה is, not where it must grow.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us (by saying...)
From any place; in any case

steps.whatToRemember: A ערבה does not need to come from beside a brook. Willows from a rain-watered field or from the mountains are also כשר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read ״נַחַל״ as a rule about location. This ברייתא teaches that the word does not limit where the willow grows.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, you may use a ערבה from any location, as long as it is the right type of willow and does not have the defects listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Willows of the brook"
phrases.notes: The plural form ״עַרְבֵי״ is what broadens the law.

phrases.english: from any place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״עַרְבֵי נַחַל״ include willows from any place, so willows from a בַּעַל field and from the mountains are valid.
